---
title: "Session 8 guided lab"
subtitle: "Boxplots, histograms, scatterplots, and export"
---

Six questions, about **50–60 minutes**. Work with a partner, take turns typing,
and write your own short answers.

## Setup

Use the supplied **synthetic marker data**: 40 participants, 20 in each arm.
One row is one participant. `baseline` and `followup` are marker measurements;
`change = followup - baseline`. The marker has no specified clinical units or
definition of improvement.

Work in **BIOS6301-mywork.Rproj**. Copy either the
[Quarto starter](starter/visualization-lab.qmd) or
[R Markdown starter](starter/visualization-lab.Rmd) from the course materials
to your personal `work/session08/` folder. Choose one format.
Run the supplied setup chunk before Q1.

## Q1. Base R boxplot

Create a **boxplot of `change` by `arm`** using `participant`.

1. Label the x-axis "Randomized arm" and the y-axis "Change in marker (follow-up minus baseline)".
2. Overlay all 40 participant values with horizontal jitter. Keep their vertical values unchanged.
3. Add a dashed horizontal line at zero.

**Answer:** Which arm has the lower median change? What does a negative change mean?

## Q2. The same boxplot with ggplot2

Create the **same `change`-by-`arm` boxplot** with ggplot2 and assign it to `p`.

1. Add `geom_boxplot()` and horizontally jittered participant points. Display each observation once.
2. Use the same axis labels and dashed zero line as Q1. Add the title "Marker change by randomized arm".
3. Add a caption: "Synthetic data; one point per participant; 20 participants per arm."

**Answer:** Do the two plots tell the same story? What do the points show that the boxes alone do not?

## Q3. Save and check your figure

Save `p` as **`change-by-arm.png` and `change-by-arm.pdf`** in an `output/` folder.

1. Use 6 × 4 inches for both files and 300 DPI for the PNG.
2. Open both files. Check the labels, caption, and participant points. Make one improvement if needed and save again.

**Answer:** What are the PNG's pixel dimensions? Why is a DPI setting unnecessary for the PDF's vector lines and text?

## Q4. Base R histogram

Use `hist()` to draw a **histogram of `baseline`** for all 40 participants.
Label the axes "Baseline marker" and "Number of participants", and add a dashed
vertical line at the sample mean.

**Answer:** Is the distribution roughly symmetric or noticeably skewed? What
does the height of a bar represent?

## Q5. Baseline versus follow-up

Use ggplot2 to make a **scatterplot of `followup` (y) versus `baseline` (x)**.
Identify `arm` with both color and shape, label both axes, and add a dashed
identity line (`y = x`). Save this plot as `p_scatter`.

**Answer:** What does a point below the line mean? Do all participants in the
treated arm have lower follow-up values than baseline?

## Q6. Compare distributions in separate panels

Use ggplot2 to make **histograms of `followup`, with one panel per `arm`**.
Use `binwidth = 0.5`, `boundary = 0`, and `facet_wrap(~ arm)`. Keep the same
x- and y-axis scales in both panels and label the axes.

**Answer:** Which arm's follow-up distribution appears centered lower? Do the
distributions overlap? Why keep the same bins and axis scales?

## Finish

Render or knit your completed report. Include the plots for **Q1, Q2, Q4,
Q5, and Q6**, short answers to **Q1–Q6**, and the Q3 export code. Keep the PNG
and PDF in `output/` beside your report. Check that all plots appear in the HTML.
Record one change made after opening the exported files, or state what you
checked if no change was needed.
